title: S4 colourings of knots are #P-hard
claim: Target: let G be a connected plane multigraph and D(G^(3)) the alternating link diagram whose Tait graph is G with every edge tripled. A full 3-twist acts trivially on pairs of reflections of S3, so the colourings of D(G^(3)) by transpositions of S3 are exactly the vertex potentials phi: V -> Z3; over phi, the colourings by transpositions of S4 form an affine space of dimension equal to the number of components of the alternating link of H_phi = (V, edges with equal potentials), which is c(H_phi) + dim B(H_phi), B the bicycle space (bicycle law). Hence the number of colourings of D(G^(3)) sending meridians to transpositions of S4 equals the number of pairs (phi, x) in (Z3 x Z2)^V with an even number of equal-phi, unequal-x edges at every vertex, equivalently 2^-n times a 12-state spin model with edge matrix J - 2N, N an involution. With every edge of G subdivided first it equals 2^-n 4^m Z_Potts(G; 12, 1/2), so counting these colourings of link diagrams is #P-hard with one query. Two-terminal series-parallel gadgets of tripled edges act through span{J, I, N} (series = product, parallel = entrywise product); substituting a gadget whose spanning trees and terminal-separating 2-forests are both odd preserves the parity of the spanning-tree count of G, hence keeps an odd-tree-count graph's diagram a knot; doubling the edges outside a spanning tree makes any connected planar graph's tree count odd without changing its chromatic polynomial; odd parallel powers of the gadget S(e,P(e,S(e,e))) give distinct bases (25/17)^i (15/17)^j, so interpolation recovers P(H,12). Hence counting homomorphisms from knot groups to S4 that send meridians to transpositions is #P-hard under Turing reductions; knot complements have first homology Z.
failure_conditions: A colouring by S3 transpositions whose number of S4 transposition lifts differs from 2^(c(H)+dim B(H)) on a tested diagram, or a colouring set not in bijection with vertex potentials.
A count that differs from the parity form, from 2^-n 4^m Z(G;12,1/2) on subdivided graphs, or from the gadget prediction on substituted graphs.
A gadget whose effective interaction differs from the algebra, or a gadget with odd tree and forest counts whose substitution into an odd-tree-count graph does not give a knot.
Interpolation that fails to recover P(H,12) from the predicted counts, or an accepted control.
foundation_claim_scope: Link and knot diagrams in S3 built as alternating diagrams of plane graphs with tripled edges; counting homomorphisms from link and knot groups to S4 that send meridians to transpositions; Turing reductions (one query for links); hardness of the planar chromatic and Potts evaluations (Vertigan) and the left-right-cycle theorem for plane graphs (Rosenstiehl and Read; Godsil and Royle) cited; closed manifolds with bounded first homology are not covered. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library, about 36 s) verifies the local lemma on the permutation table, the bicycle law on every colouring of 19 plane graphs (potential bijection, lift dimension = F2 Laplacian nullity, left-right cycles = c + dim B), the parity, twelve-state and Potts(12, 1/2) identities with link components 1 + beta1 on nine graphs, the gadget algebra and the spanning-tree formula on all series-parallel gadgets up to 4 and 5 edges, knot preservation exactly for odd tree and forest counts, end-to-end knot counts on four substituted graphs, recovery of P(H,12) by interpolation for K4, C5 and the diamond, and four controls. No human or external review
